Adequate provision should be made to consider and weigh the benefits, costs and possible adverse effects of various proposed uses before making final decisions on the proposed dedication of such areas for the protection of threatened or endangered species of wildlife, to the exclusion or prohibition of other uses of the area.
Also, the draft environmental statement makes no provision for the removal of species from threatened or endangered lists when such action is justified by changing conditions, increased population levels, or other factors. Such provision should be made to make available for other uses portions of areas which had been barred to other uses by their dedication to the protection of threatened or endangered species.
Also, just as the proposed legislation provides for public acquisition of areas and the imposition of legal controls and restrictions to accomplish the purposes of the Act, there should be provision for the release of areas from such dedication, or from public ownership, and the modification of legal controls and restrictions when they are no longer required or justified for the protection of threatened or endangered species.
